perspective:
Christian’s available information:

- He is a police officer. Jonathan is his close childhood friend; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian had been feeling Jonathan was hiding something important. He observed Jonathan acting differently, which made him anxious and suspicious.
- Christian arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop and confronted him.
- Christian heard Jonathan admit that he had been keeping something from him, that he was in some trouble, and that he hadn’t known how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic, offered his help and support, and said they could face the situation together.
- Christian heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated and that he didn’t want to drag Christian into it. Jonathan also accepted Christian’s support/resources and said he needed to figure a way out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was related to anything illegal.
- Christian heard Jonathan say he couldn’t be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he didn’t do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decided to look into the matter discreetly to make sure Jonathan was safe. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through Christian’s investigation, he came to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up.
- Christian told Jonathan he had leads but was not sure yet who was responsible. He decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later found out/believes the person behind it is someone close to both him and Jonathan—someone they both know and trust. He feels betrayed and resolute.
- Christian told Jonathan he intended to confront the culprit and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous but said he trusted Christian to do what is right.
- Christian has identified the culprit, though the provided dialogue does not name that person.

Excluded: hidden events, private thoughts/feelings of Jonathan not stated to Christian, narrator-only facts beyond what Christian observed, heard, was told, investigated, or did himself.
